“Welcome to the space market! The largest, most impressive, one hundred percent Kraken free market in space! Report any Kraken or Mastermind presence to security immediately.” The pre-recorded welcome message hails in from the station's short range communication array. You see the small mining vessel that you followed here docked at another platform and struggle to recall the actual route that led you here, but this thought quickly fades before the spectacle that is the space market, its unyielding energy stirring a burnin desire in you to go on a spending frenzy.
The spinning of the station starts to wear on you, a sickening, syrup-like gravity being generated that far exceeds that which was present on Earth. The local species that seem to govern the station look comfortabl as though they had evolved within such a strong ﬁ eld of gravity. Feeling like a wrestler after a heavy workout, yo hobble through the arrangement of shops...
You sell an old tape recorder and other useless gadgets from Earth that catch the hungry eyes of the alien broke you pass. Gain 7¢.
You can now trade at a Shop and Ammo Dealer to buy an sell Weapons. Their grade is deﬁ ned in slot A of the Line Variables. You may also use a Modder and a Gambler.
A: Finish your business and then leave the station.
B: Try to sell knowledge about Earth’s technology and th human race to get some extra credits.
01:
You carefully explore new areas of the star system avoiding the presence of the Mastermind and its Kraken minions as best you can. An unexpected ﬁ nd comes in th form of a quiet, weary little Spanish spaceship. The singl occupant tells you a tale of an unidentiﬁ ed virus that decimated their crew. As the ship's medical ofﬁ cer they were able to produce an antidote, but not soon enough to save their friend Maik who was the ﬁ rst to fall ill, nor their previous captain. The medic is adamant the virus is gone now, though you note a desperate optimism in his voice. Spaceships aren't great places to be trapped with a virus in any situation. He informs you that he's coming over to join your crew and insists that the antidote he has will protect your crew from the virus. You can’t brin yourself to condemn this man, so you allow him in throug the airlock.
He introduces himself and hands you some credits as a sign of gratitude, along with a memory card containing coordinates of a secret wormhole leading to an ancient star system. He says he won it gambling, even betting their spaceship whilst the captain and crew were out getting drunk. The Grey who lost the gamble wasn't too happy about it and broke out into a rage, so the medic decided to drag his drunk friends back on board their sh and ﬂ ee before the Greys caught them.
Gain 5¢. Gain 'Nikoluka' as a new Crew Member. He can be found in the Crew Proﬁ les section of the rulebook. If Nikoluka is already in your crew, you instead gain anothe preset Crew member of your choice. In both cases the new Crew Member has no Equipment. If you already have 4 Crew Members, you can either replace an existing Cre Member or decline to take Nikoluka into your party with other effects.
02:
Your departure from Earth was grueling, the loss of your family weighing heavily on your every thought.
Your studies in Europe had been cut short when you heard that the Kraken was attacked with nuclear weapons at the city where your family lived, which destroyed virtually everything and killing everyone. For this you bear a deep hatred of the Kraken and have vowed to correct the course of history by erasing this beast from existence.
This was the ﬁ rst thought as you looked back on the g devastated planet Earth, and you accept that it may be your last thought in your ﬁ nal moments.
If you only have one Crew Member, stop reading here and progress this Story Line.
e, As your journey proceeds you suffer harsh nightmares and struggle with your duties onboard the ship. Shortly u after the incident during which your ship was dragged through a wormhole, you enter into another nightmare, one in which a member of the Crew has been driven psychotic, and you catch them about to kill another rs sleeping Crew Member. You lunge for the nearest weapon and land a wild shot in their leg, preventing one death just in time, but sadly the deranged crew member bleeds d profusely, and soon dies. The entire crew is on edge as you wait to wake from the nightmare, but it never comes.
At least the experience teaches your Crew a valuable lesson; nothing in this insane universe can truly be trusted. You spare a thought for yet another victim of e the void.
Erase one Crew Member (other than your Leader), keeping , their Equipment if you wish. You receive 26 XP.

You have two theories; either some alien anomaly is removing random items from your ship, or a member of your Crew is stealing things. You gather the crew and try to uncover some clue as to the source of the missing inventory items. g Suddenly, the beverage dispenser can be heard from h another room. no The creature doesn't seem to be present, until you notice a small tentacle on the shoulder of the crew member still attempting to restrain you. It meanders gently around their head as though familiar with the shape. It is without doubt the tentacle of a Kraken, though a very small one.

07:
You search for a merchant or some other place where you might get your hands on a few extra credits, coming across what appears to be some sort of museum or archive. You're anxious to devise a good plan for this system, but decide that for now it couldn't hurt to go inside the structure and have a look around.
As you stroll through the halls adorned with various strange items, someone unknown draws close to you and begins to talk very quietly. 08:
As your journey continues you encounter an independent planet controlled by a species called the Krakruk, a world close to the asteroid ﬁ eld further out into the system, well outside the current Kraken territory. You land there to get some supplies and ﬁ nd the locals are helpful and welcoming, despite what seems to be a very strict local culture with bans on alcohol, drugs, slavery and cloning being illustrated on various signs dotted around. There also seems to be a strong presence of police ships patrolling the world, watching the movements of the inhabitants. Coincidentally you're given a tip-off about a cloning facility from some unhinged alien who seems to be obsessed with human physiology and keeps reminding you "there's always a need for more test subjects".

09:
Your efforts only serve to further weaken the Morrocks' already shaky faith in your loyalty. They are unwilling to forgive the Mejang and seem to have decided on a risky, somewhat desperate course of action judging from their tone, announcing their plans for domination of Aeus and expansion outwards into the wider world as well.
A group of Morrock guards are summoned to escort you out of Aeus.
Whilst you knew this was a possible outcome, it still comes as a surprise. You think back to the well-humored, large eyed children who would always celebrate your arrival. As you approach your ship you spot Mufty nearby. His gaze is sad as he watches you board your ship.
0A:
You spot a tiny object approaching, passing you by in the blink of an eye and disappearing before you can catch sight of it. With so little light in this part of space you can't even guess at what it was. Your equipment detects only a low energy signature.
Read the following clue ONLY if you have a Crew Member with the PSI Trait:
One of your PSI-capable crew members seems distracted, suddenly twisting their head as if to look back at the object. "It's alive.. sentient. Wait... it's.. human! There's a person in there! They're not awake though, they're dreaming."

0B:
Following the Mejang's advice you trek north through dense vegetation and after two hours you ﬁ nally come across a settlement. A wall looms over you with what appears to be a defensive tower, an insect-like being stationed at the top.
You enter through a gate as the insect-like Morrocks welcome you, guiding you towards their city after you mention your crew needing food and a place to rest.
As you walk, you keep your eyes and ears open for any information that could be useful to the Mejang, but you note nothing more than relatively civilized humanoid insects going about surprisingly familiar daily routines.
Occasionally you draw the attention of a curious Morrock as they inspect your appearance, playing with your hair and intrigued by the pliability of your skin. You suspect they don't get many human visitors and you must be as strange and unusual to them as a society of 2m tall talking bugs is to you.
They seem happy to welcome you into their city, and you respectfully tolerate their curiosity. Smaller individuals hover nearby, children you suspect, intrigued by your presence as they follow you with large, faceted eyes.
Your plan was that they would be eager for information about the world beyond their own borders, information you can easily gather, and that might be something they are willing to compensate you for. This seems like an increasingly realistic plan given the amount of interest they are taking in you. They emphasize that you are welcome to sleep, eat and hide among them inside Aeus whenever you wish, so long as you keep it a secret. They seem peaceful, certainly towards you, but they probably have a lot to gain from earning your appreciation. You consider how to make the most of the situation:
A: Offer to spy on the Mejang and report back to the Morrocks to support them in the conﬂ ict.
B: Work on building a few connections and offering your services as a point of contact with the outside world, should the Morrocks need any goods or other resources.
0C:
Heading into a mound of scrap metal and down long heat-cut corridors you enter into a cave. A giant humanoid spots you and spares no time in welcoming you to the 'Lightning Dome' through the breathing device that obscures their entire face. At ﬁ rst you are on edge, unsure of what you've found, but a glance around the cave suggests this is a being very much devoted to their work.
The walls are lined with strange devices, blast holes and burnt rock, and the occupant seems almost as haggard as the cave. They seem to note your curious expression as they declare their love for both collecting and modding weapons, as well as a good gamble whenever they get the chance.
You may interact with the resident of the Lightning Dome as a Gambler and/or Modder. He functions as would a Gambler or Modder found during normal exploration.
Once you conclude your business with the nameless giant you bid them farewell, reﬂ ecting on what strange lives some beings live. You make your way out of the scrap 'facility'.

0F:
Somewhere in the void of space:
Screaming, she wakes suddenly. Covered in sweat, she glances at her clock to again ﬁ nd that she's woken at 3am, two hours before her watch shift is due to start, and angrily slams her hands into the bed. She's freezing cold from the sweat and the chill air that resides in the ship. She grows increasingly angry at her situation, night after night waking in terror due to dreams she can't even remember. It's hard to think, sleep deprivation and constant cold-ache distracting her every thought.
The ship's medical specialist hasn't been able to help. The problem is the dream, whatever it is, that she can never recall... At least, she thinks it's a dream. She closes her eyes and concentrates, grasping at the fading memories of whatever it was that startled her. She knows that she was trying to save someone, maybe someone she loves?
It couldn't be someone she loves. Everyone she loved was taken from her long ago. But she did remember the odd feeling, something about the dream, something that made it feel like she was truly living it. It even made her scream.
Or did it? Did she scream? She can hear it in her head, her voice. Was it her voice?
She glances at the clock again, 3:02am, a ﬂ ash of anger and exasperation at her recurring problem. Then she realizes that she's already looked at the clock, but can't remember the last two minutes. She struggles to recall, but the harder she tries, the further the memory of her dream slips away. Was she even trying to save someone at all? She concentrates harder as her brow furrows in the effort. She can hear the scream. Louder this time.
The scream is so clear now, and getting louder.
Suddenly she springs up, pounces over to her cabin door. Now, she presses her ear to the door and listens intently. The scream is approaching, seemingly from the corridor outside her room. She quickly snatches her riﬂ e and slams the door button. With a high-pitched swoosh the door rapidly slides open. She is immediately drawn to a ﬁ gure running towards her a few meters down the corridor. The ﬁ gure's gait is terrifying, most likely because they are entirely engulfed in ﬂ ames. Instinctively she raises her weapon to ﬁ re at the approaching individual, unable to make out who it might be. In the second she is given, she hesitates and fails to ﬁ re her weapon, knowing that ﬁ ring weapons inside spaceships is a fairly sure way to end everyone's day badly.
Fortunately this didn't condemn her to a ﬂ aming death, as the apparently male ﬁ gure bounces past her, taking a sudden right turn just past her doorway and crashing into a bulkhead with enough force to knock themselves out.
The screaming stops sharply and the ﬂ aming mass lies there quietly, barely distinguishable as human.
Other crew members start cautiously poking their heads out of their cabins to see what all the commotion is about. She notes that whilst some crew members jump into action, grabbing ﬁ re extinguishers and offering what medical assistance they can, several also seem to freeze, unable to do anything of use . She's only been under A Crowther's command for 3 weeks now, but it seems this crew has a knack for drawing in misfortune. She decides that tonight she'll grab a shuttle and put this cursed crew and ship behind her.

0O:
You revisit the 'Lightning Dome' under the scrap mound to see if the masked giant would like to gamble , with you, but the sound of a ship landing in the distance distracts you both. 0P:
On your return to Aeus you notice Mufty, the giant worm. This is the ﬁ rst time you've seen him on the surface and from this distance he could almost be mistaken for distant mountains. You notice a wreckage not far in front of Mufty, ﬂ ames spouting from it and a humanoid creature jumping around in a rage. Mufty watches with what you think might be a hint of sadness, though as giant worms go you can't really tell what he's feeling. As you set down your ship nearby, Mufty begins what will be a slow hour's slither back down the hole he must have emerged from.
As you approach, the owner of the craft notices you and adopts a calmer demeanor. They introduce themselves as 'Axel the Machine Master', explaining that they were exploring the hole when that monster emerged from the fog, startling them. You suspect he probably crashed his ship trying to make a rapid exit from the hole, since Mufty isn't exactly pretty. Axel goes on to explain how he survived by landing on the beast's face, which then deposited him on the surface just outside the hole. A burst of ﬂ ame startles you both as it erupts from the engine.
The entire ship was deformed like a crushed soda can, but Axel shrugs it off and says he could ﬁ x it with a few spare parts.

B: Save the spare parts. You never know when you will need them yourself. Wish Axel the Machine Master good luck and tell him to play dead if Maggie shows up, as she can be very playful. You decide not to mention that she's an infant giant worm.
0Q:
Docking at a grafﬁ ti coated trading station, you blend in with the various strange aliens and creatures coming and going and enter without issue. You suspect as a human it would be best not to draw anyone's attention, even in a place like this. It's an ideal hiding place though, a gathering point of the various outcasts struggling to enjoy their lives under the tough conditions of the Mastermind’s domain. The variety of alien species here suggests that there are more systems than just this and Earth that have been imprisoned in Death Spheres.
You decide to make the most of the various lawless, untaxed markets and shops selling everything from instant soups to plasma riﬂ es. It seems to be a paradise for tech nerds. You may Trade with a grade 2 Shop.
As you continue exploring the markets, you ﬁ nd a store selling a sculpture of a space station in miniature scale for just 7¢. You could buy it legitimately, try to sweet talk the owner, or just try to steal it despite the attention of multiple other store owners being on you.
You may buy the 'Miniature Space Station' for 7¢.
With a Crew Member of your choice you can make a single Charisma Check against 8+ and if you pass, you haggle the price down to 3¢.
With a Crew Member of your choice you can make a single Agility Check against 9+. If you pass you steal the Item, but if you fail this Event ends.
0R: They appreciate your offer and enjoy a pleasant evening. The next morning you leave Aeus, planning to soon return and see how they are doing.
0S:
Five days and ﬁ ve nights later the Mejang and the Morrocks sign their ﬁ rst peace treaty in a surprisingly modest ceremony. A somewhat terrible memorial statue to you and your crew is unveiled to much applause.
Celebrations last for over a week. Even Mufty crawls near the city, surprisingly carefully, without destroying many miles of agricultural land. Nobody is even frightened by his presence. Whilst it seems it will take a while for the two species to fully embrace this new arrangement, both sides seem open to it. Their leaders speak of the beneﬁ ts of unity, turning their attentions to the outer worlds, and standing together against the Mastermind.

They present a tribute, seemingly all the wealth they could spare. They also offer what information and counsel they can, after which you reﬂ ect on the positive impact you've had on this planet, which at one point might not have been far from complete annihilation. As you take the tribute back to your ship they bid you farewell, insisting you visit them again soon. Gain 200¢ and 20 XP.
0T:
You wonder what depths this rabbit hole might extend to as the space station's main elevator takes you deeper and deeper, far beyond the living disc to a citadellike structure at what feels to be the underside of the station. The strange alien guides you to a ﬂ oor of shops that seem more like display stands for a variety of weird and unique collections, of which the owners all seem to be very proud to own. As you explore you note that the traders are very inquisitive and do not shy away from asking questions, at one point one even offering to buy one of your ﬁ ngers.
Unusual and outright inexplicable products aren't something human markets tend to shy away from, but you're still taken aback by the curious sights before you.
Slaves of all kinds are available for purchase along with numerous tools and objects the likes of which you've never seen before. You are offered a disturbingly low amount of credits in exchange for one of your crew members by someone looking for sentient beings to perform live experiments on, an offer you courteously decline so as to not offend whatever customs they might have in this place.
At the next stall a three-eyed frowning alien catches your attention with his collection of frozen creatures, one of which is clearly a human. The vendor claims it's the ﬁ rst human that was found in this system. He appears to be frozen, though the vendor clariﬁ es that he doesn't know how to revive this speciﬁ c individual or if it would even be possible at this point. You take a look at the box and the frozen human within. It seems the container is similar to all the other articles and is probably something the vendor constructs to store their 'products', though it's rudimentary and uninteresting in its design. The occupant is much more interesting. The face is very familiar, someone you're certain you saw on Earth once. He still wears an astronaut suit, the name still imprinted and easily readable, 'Maximilian P'. It's not a familiar name.
As you continue explore this bizarre bazaar two things eventually catch your curiosity; 1) The doctor who offered to buy your crew member is selling parasitic worms in little glass tubes. The labels explain that they attach to the brain after insertion through the nose and enable the adoption of PSI powers.
There is a warning scribbled out, but it seems to mention something about death. If you have no Crew Member with the PSI Trait you may pay 10¢ to pick a Crew Member with a free Trait slot and roll a d6.
On a 1: Erase the Crew Member. You may keep their Equipment.
On a 2: Nothing happens.
On a 3+: Give the chosen Crew the PSI Trait at Level 1.
2) Somebody asks you for a Rotten Ngngnam Egg, apparently taking a complete shot in the dark at ﬁ nding one. If you are willing to sell him one to add to his insane collection of strange eggs he offers to pay you handsomely. He talks a lot about the heavenly, transcendental taste of this egg and understands that you would want to keep such a delicacy for your own consumption, and thus his offer is indeed generous. You may discard 'Rotten Ngngnam Egg' to gain 50¢.
Unfortunately you don't ﬁ nd anything that might help you forget all the unsettling and grotesque things you've seen in this place, so once you're done looking you leave and try to think happy thoughts.

Long range sensors detect a small capsule nearby, one that appears to be a common model found on many of the ships that departed Earth. There are no other vessels near it, so you move in to take a closer look. After about 30 minutes of inspecting it, the capsule seems to respond to your communication attempts and sends an emergency signal via directional radio transmission. After a little maneuvering you bring the capsule onto your ship, and once you've restored the atmosphere you open the capsule. It’s a woman from Earth, Bellatrix Prosperine, who recalls a Kraken attack on her ship and her hurried escape. She had no time to save the rest of the crew and was the only one lucky enough to already be near the capsule bays.
You get the impression there's something she's not telling you, but she still seems trustworthy. Maybe she stole the capsule in order to escape some other, more human threat?
If you wanted to, you could tell her that your food and oxygen supplies are depleted and that her odds of survival are much better in the capsule. If you do this, add 3 to your Interlink’s variable R.
If you do not do this, add Bellatrix Prosperine to your crew, or if she's already part of it, gain a new Crew Member. You may replace one of your existing Crew Members if you do not have an available Crew slot. She will come with her starting Equipment and her Level will match that of your highest Level Crew Member, apply the appropriate number of Level up bonuses now too. If you already have a Crew Member with the PSI Trait when adding her, erase the Trait from Bellartix Prosperine and replace it with a different positive Trait of your choice.
In either case you continue on with your journey. If you add Bellatrix Prosperine to your crew, you can read the below text:
She puts effort into contributing around the ship and any Crew she replaced will leave your ship at the next station, a melancholy event that you put behind you as best you can.

11:
Since you aren't especially practiced at stealing things, you decide to use a distraction to draw the attention of any guards or potential witnesses. One of your crew fakes some health issue, falling onto the ﬂ oor screaming and shaking rapidly. The others open the unshielded showcase and take the artifact which looks like a stick with a handle and some tree-like structure made of ﬁ bers on the other side. It looks dirty, but since it's a museum exhibit you decide it's best not to try and clean it until you know what it is. With the artifact in a huge bag you make for the exit but notice that security is already alert to the theft and are quickly moving towards you.
The guards look small, but quite angry. You either need to outrun their surprisingly fast pace, or ﬁ nd some way of incapacitating them.
Each of your Crew Members must make a Strength or Agility Check against 8+. Each Crew Member that fails loses 3 HP (Armor and Shields are not applied) and then repeats the check (until they pass or run out of HP). If somehow your entire Crew is knocked out by this, your Campaign is over; they wake in some unmarked prison cell serving an unknown sentence, one surely too long for you to complete your mission.
If at least one Crew Member passes, all of your Crew make it back to the ship regardless of HP, leaving the raging security guards behind with no apparent means of pursuit. You and your companions agree it's probably best to not return to this place for a good while. This space pirate lifestyle isn't something you're sure you'll get used to, but you at least feel wiser for the experience. Gain 5xp.
A day later you arrive at the meeting place to make the trade with the shifty collector and get your reward. You grow more and more suspicious as time passes, and a whole day has soon gone by with nothing to show for it but irritation. You accept that you probably aren't going to get paid for the artifact, so you decide to keep it in order to ﬁ nd a buyer. You're wary of this option since it's the kind of thing that might attract space pirates, but also because the museum may have sent out agents to search for the stolen item. Despite this, you can't just throw it away after the risk you took to get it. The dirty stick thing isn't only quite ugly, it's also quite large and seemingly fragile, so you make sure to give it lots of padding space to protect it. The 'Dirty Artifact' occupies two slots of your Ship's storage. If you do not have space you MUST discard Items until you do.

13:
Your mind r esists a million atomic reactions before it collapses and for a moment you feel nothing. An intense pain is then swept aside by a ﬂ ood of knowledge as the A.I.
updates the newly established computing infrastructure within your mind. You immediately feel that some tired, inefﬁ cient part of your mind has been removed, replaced with something new, some part of your conscience that makes sense now.
You may increase up to 3 of your Leader's Attributes by up to 2 points each, the maximum value in this case being 9. They also gain the PSI Trait at Level 4. If they already have the PSI Trait at a lower Level, it becomes Level 4.

As you return to your ship, you become aware of a pack of primitive creatures following closely behind you. You at ﬁ rst assume they are lost, but then recall that they have been following you for quite some time now, unable to ﬁ nd their own way. With resentment you recall the small questions they ask and the irrelevant ideas they present, the laziness with which they move. Even their scent now seems stupid, inelegant, basic.
As you step into the high speed elevator to return to your ship, a spontaneous decision drives you to launch the elevator before these creatures are able to board it with you. You can't afford to look after them anymore, you have more important things to do. This will be a good experience for them, to teach them to adapt and deal with their situation themselves. What you're doing for them is a kindness.
Once you board your ship you launch without pause, no thought given for the crew you just left behind.
Apart from your Leader, erase all of your Crew Members, including their Inventory.
Emotional attachments aren't of any beneﬁ t to you. Your crew are a set of living tools that can be modiﬁ ed and replaced to suit your needs. If emotions were effective, the species of this universe wouldn't perpetually struggle with such simple things as basic needs and self-fulﬁ llment. You're conﬁ dent your wisdom will allow you to assemble a much more efﬁ cient crew, completely obedient and committed to serving your ambitions. The arrangement will be optimal.

Likely thousands of years old, the low gravity of the planet seems to have enabled the tree to grow to an insane size and obscure the archive from view, even when standing directly in front of it. You're aware that another craft is still following you and is likely to arrive soon, however you're not too concerned with this as you remember the diabololike shape.
You ﬁ nd evidence that Adam was here and that a resistance is forming against the Mastermind. There are also various blueprints that seem to detail alien technologies, which you and your team take some interesting notes from. Gain 5 XP.
The librarian, an old woman in a white dress, appears and starts making chit chat with you, seeming very eager to make the most of some intelligent company. You attempt to gather some additional information from the librarian.
If you have an unused Story Line and a Crew Member with the PSI Trait OR pass a Charisma Check against 7+ with a Crew Member of your choice (you only get one attempt), note the coordinate 2KC on an unused Story Line. Skip it during this game turn's 'Activate Lines' phase.
Then the Bayjuy then enter the hall, the librarian immediately ordering them to leave and mentioning that they caused complete chaos the last time they were here.

As quickly as that feeling arrives, it leaves again.
You feel like you missed out on something, something big maybe. Clouds can contain basically anything, so you consider that maybe it was just some stray neurostimulants that managed to leak in through the ventilation system. Since you arrived at this star system you seem to ﬁ nd two more questions for each one your answer, and you know you don't have time to ﬁ nd answers for all of them.
1A: You suspect it would be better if you didn't hand out important information about Earth, but show your gratitude for the repairs by recalling as many menial details about Earth life as you can manage.
1B: Your escape is dramatically close. As you hurriedly make your way out of the dark tunnels, you see thousands of insect-like monsters in pursuit of your crew. You make it back to safety just in time, shivering at the thought of what might have happened had those creatures caught you.
1C:
As you leave Aeus you are invited into a shop you'd never noticed, the owner offering you anything you can compensate them for, in addition to sharing some information they'd come by. You may Trade at a grade 6 Shop.
As you browse their products the shopkeeper walks alongside you.
"The Death Sphere around the entire star system is powered by a well-hidden and protected generator at the core of KLEBER 2, another planet in this star system.
This planet was colonized by the Kraken forces as soon as they'd arrived and has been under their control ever since. It seems however that there is a way to destroy or at least interrupt the generator, and thus the Death Sphere. A message from Adam was forwarded to this station suggesting that hacking a single control console should be enough to deactivate the generator, and the Death Sphere, at least for a while."
Despite the risks, you decide that you can't afford to pass up an opportunity like this. The Mastermind's control seems to be ever-expanding and you don't suspect you'll be able to cut a deal with it once its inﬂ uence reaches you.
Once you ﬁ nish trading with the shop you prepare your ship for the task ahead and get ready to depart.
After days of travel at a reduced energy signature you arrive at KLEBER 2, managing to enter its atmosphere without detection by exploiting your ship's small size and powering down the majority of its systems. The descent to the surface is intense as you guide the craft downwards, guiding it by manually operating the crudely assembled rudders you built speciﬁ cally for this task.
You level the ship out so its underbelly generates as much air resistance as possible, whilst keeping an eye on the portholes to keep track of the rapidly approaching surface. You'll need to ﬁ re the retro-boosters you've attached at the exact right moment to safely land the ship. Without the ship's complex computing, you had to use some old Earth calculation equipment you found in storage to work out the numbers yourself. One wrong calculation might tear the ship apart as you ﬁ re unevenly balanced rockets, but at this point you can only hope your calculations are accurate.
Seconds before impact with the surface you ﬁ re off the retro rockets as the crew slumps down into their seats.
The burn-off guides the ship down to the ground, landing awkwardly on its nose at ﬁ rst, then settling down gently enough that no signiﬁ cant damage is caused.
As you scout out the control station you note only a single team of guards stationed there, however they look exceptionally well prepared. There's no time to waste, even your small spacecraft has a signiﬁ cant visual proﬁ and could be spotted by scouting parties at any moment Initiate a Ground Combat with Level 7 Enemies (L.Diff.

1I:
You are surprised to receive a video transmission n, from an older woman, who introduces herself as Samira, a a friend of the librarian you met some time ago. You recognize how you've grown increasingly tense with each transmission you receive, each alien species has a different culture and quirks. Typical human gestures such as waving or revealing your palms could mean anything s from a declaration of war to an invitation to a romantic dinner where your crew is on the menu. But this time an old looking human woman leaves you feeling more relaxed as she explains that she was born in Morocco, but has been stranded in this region for a very long time.
She veers off into tales of how she used to tell stories to children on a poor little moon planet, but eventually comes back to the subject of her support for other humans and for the resistance efforts of Adam and others. She claims a many wish to form a resistance, many more wanting m simply to escape the Death Sphere surrounding this and the other systems. She says she's visited three other star systems which were also caught in Death Spheres and regardless of the environment or the native species, the Mastermind's power is always overwhelming.
Samira is about to share a secret about the Mastermind before she's interrupted by a couple of kids asking for lunch. She promises to call back soon and says goodbye as several small alien hands wave in her face.

You feel a welcoming familiarity as you return to the grafﬁ ti-station and the usual worn out pre-recorded messages greet you. You note that many of the stalls and stores have again expanded their wares. You may Trade at a grade 5 Shop.
This time you notice a collector of stuffed creatures. If you own a 'Stuffed Killer Pumpkin', the collector turns yellow with excitement as you ﬂ aunt it in front of them.

1K:
Dr Leigh accompanies you back to your ship in the highest spirits. He's so enamored with ideas of the future with his new friends that he doesn't question it when you ask him to wait in the airlock whilst you rearrange some of the ship's furniture to make space for Leigh's huge body. With the slug monster sitting in the airlock you take off and orient the ship so that the airlock door is directly facing the searing sun. With a single command your crew thrusts the ship forward at full power and opens the airlock door at the same time. You hear an unnatural sound before checking to make sure the plan worked and see a long, smoldering body drifting towards the sun, shuddering as the heat cooks it alive.
A few hours pass and you notice that the mimic has gone dormant and won't even follow basic commands now. A member of the crew speculates that she might have relied on some telepathic connection with Dr. Leigh, which you admit could be possible. She's still technically alive so you place her into a deep sleep capsule, but you're doubtful she'll ever recover consciousness
1L:
Ewar and Aleora look at each other, then smile as they begin a transformation, their physiology becoming increasingly similar to that of a human. The leader's meetings have been canceled for some annual celebration, though as a Morrock celebration you don't suspect it would be of much interest to you. You decide to make this a short visit and get back to your other tasks.
1N:

You're much closer this time and able to detect a series of mine shafts beneath the moon's surface, apparently abandoned before their resources had been extracted. A lot of the equipment still seems to be at its station, ready to resume mining. Something about the situation feels very eerie.

B: Avoid the moon.
1P:
A transmission comes through from an unknown location:
Adam, transmission #4:
“Even now as I focus towards my new goal, I miss Max so very much. I no longer fear death as long as there is any chance it would unite us again. He was the only one who ever understood me, the love of my life, even though I never dared to tell him. I was a coward. I must not give up and allow others to fall into the Mastermind's grip. I will punish this creature for what it has done to me and to its many other victims. Perhaps I will cut it into pieces and put it back together just to cut it back into pieces again and again until the end of time. I will spend what remains of my life crashing down on this foul creature like the tsunami once sent to wash all evil from the face of the Earth". A breathless pause ﬁ nishes the burning rant.
"I hear of a time where these innocent worlds saw peace, before the arrival of this foul creature, before it locked these star systems in spheres of death. I remind you that he is not very talkative; he kills, dominates and delights in torturing everything which has a soul.
I dream of the day I hear of the Mastermind's demise. I would sacriﬁ ce the pleasure of destroying it myself if it meant I could live in a time without its presence. But I know this is a dangerous dream. This creature has deﬁ ed all laws of nature, something unnatural between mortality and godliness, meddling with the nature of reality. Do not ﬁ ght alone. There is always a way for this creature to defeat you, and it always ﬁ nds it. For those of you that can, ﬂ ee, leave forever and save what you can of your culture, your history and your souls.
Whatever you do, do not use nuclear weaponry. I must also sadly admit that the Mastermind has all my knowledge of Earth too. Those of you who know me know that I would never give up this information willingly, but will is no barrier to the Mastermind.
I don't know what motivates this warped being, what we might use to reason with it, but when it invaded my mind I felt that it was proud and wanted to brag about its immense power and cunning schemes. I do not know if it feeds on suffering or is driven by a fear of anything that might pose a threat to it. Disturbingly, I think the latter may be the more dire situation. I think it knows at this point that it is an enemy of virtually all living things. If it cannot trust anything, it must control everything.
Residents of the universe, I leave you with these 5 pieces of advice; One, if you see something that has tentacles, kill it. These creatures cannot know loyalty, love or compassion. There's no bargaining with this being, and no one is going to beat it alone. Fourthly, if you somehow escape the Death Spheres, ﬂ ee and seek help, don't try to return and help others who are trapped. Lastly, if anyone returns to Earth by some miracle, please tell anybody who might remember me that I am sorry.
Adam."

As your ship ﬁ ghts the force of the explosion to stay its course, you soon reach the recorded position of the Death Sphere. You release a small capsule you've prepared with some creatures inside. It manages to leave the star system beyond the point where once every living cell would have melted away as they passed the Death Sphere's ﬁ eld. You prepare your ship for battle, intending to ﬁ ght alongside the escape ships you're not even sure will be armed for combat. You remain in position for what feels like hours, not entirely sure whether you should just ﬂ ee and leave everyone to fend for themselves.
As the unfathomably large ﬂ eet approaches you, you notice that the ships have all sorts of designs, and all of them are prepared for battle. It must be a backup ﬂ eet, destroying the escape ships without any resistance.
You stop suddenly, stunned as you start to pick up various transmissions from the other escaping ships.
"What? Is this a joke? Is this the Kraken backup ﬂ eet?
Someone blow that dumba** out the way…”
"Oh hey, we're kinda escaping a tyrannical super-being so if you're looking for some sightseeing, you probably wanna head in some other direction."

d “I must start at the beginning, millions of years ago. Life e arose on countless planets in a multitude of galaxies and universes. The strongest species became increasingly intelligent and developed their technology whilst all others n eventually perished. Through their evolution these species r grew to value the subjugation of all other species."

Some servants bring drinks for you and the queen, who takes a sip before continuing.
“Around 5,500 years ago as the understanding of t teleportation and wormhole technology was solidiﬁ ed, a s debate was held to decide whether this technology should grant immortality to its users, transferring their minds to a digital backup during teleportation.
Early attempts at teleportation involved sending matter atom by atom and re-assembling it at the destination. For this to work living tissue would have to be sent nearlyinstantly, or it would die. To be able to move matter at this speed would require an unimaginable amount of energy, so a different approach was taken. Through technology still only partially understood, it became possible to fold 'space' to alter the positional relationship between different locations, then allowing matter to be pushed instantly between those two places. Whilst effective, this could not be used as a means of cloning, because to enter the new location the matter still has to leave the old location. Many think cloning stations work this way, but they actually use bodies grown and genetically modiﬁ ed in tanks.
Virtual mind uploads have long been impossible, for it is required that the exact structure and electrical state of the mind be analyzed, which must be done in a single instant so that the process does not disturb the structure of the subject's consciousness, which would cause the process to fail. This issue was eventually overcome through the use of a unique form of wormhole technology.
By using an array of micro-wormholes each particle of a brain, spinal cord and nerve tracts can be dispensed into one of several trillion small chambers containing scanning equipment. The device is active for only a few picoseconds, trillionths of a second, recording the state of every single cell of brain and central nerve tissue before they die off and are ejected. Due to the death of the original organic tissue, the process cannot be reversed.
The mind continues its awareness from then on as a virtual entity.
A supercomputer then makes various minute adjustments, guided by deep learning developed from its records of all uploaded minds, with the aim of maintaining and if possible, improving the performance and structure of the uploaded consciousness. This is its one and only aim, to preserve and optimize the uploaded mind.”

You can't tell what's wrong, but it's bugging you. You stare at the scanner interface, certain that you were in a completely different place not ﬁ ve minutes ago. You blink and one of the stars is gone. Or was it never there? You check the monitor for any dirt, check the equipment's energy supply. Suddenly stars shift position, then return after a moment. The display module seems ﬁ ne, but some part of the equipment is deﬁ nitely having trouble. You've got some time to spare, so you grab a suit and climb out onto the hull of the ship to check the sensor array. As you're approaching it you pause, frozen.
The stars are actually shifting in space, jumping from one place to another, almost dancing. You turn around, questioning your sanity, but the ship turns with you. No...
it hasn't turned, this is the front. You frantically look back at the front of the ship, and then around again at the front of the ship, then back again to see the... you see yourself standing a few meters away, looking at an endless column of yourself. You fall, or ﬂ oat maybe? You feel the hull of the ship, take comfort in the 'plonk' sound as you gently bounce your ﬁ st against it. You must have been exposed to a toxin at some point. You radio for medical assistance through your suit's radio system.
"You're doing good, keep working, you'll be with us shortly.
You have no idea whose voice that is. Your sight is completely warped, planets popping open like rotten oranges, stars, ﬂ ickering like light bulbs on an old train.
And there's this one star, it's so damn bright. Everything else moving, stuttering, but this star is still, growing, brighter than your mind can comprehend. You realize what this is now. A white hole. A dimensional ﬁ ssure, a pathway to another dimension. You think over all of the chaos, the pain and fear of this universe, the Kraken, the Death Spheres, all of it. Hell, how bad can a change of scenery be if it's absolutely nothing like this? You relax, watching as your ship gradually drifts into the light.
You pass out... or, maybe... maybe you wake up. You can't remember how long you were out... or in? It's very confusing, despite that everything is perfectly clear.
You wake in a familiar room, one you've never seen before. You feel your skin prickling, as though the air is bombarding it with tiny little rockets. You can feel the world around you. You hear a familiar voice, a radio transmission somewhere in the background; "My name is Adam. If you are stranded in this system, I have an important warning for you...". Things seem to be going unexpectedly well. You arrive at a new location to hear that Kraken forces have recently abandoned the region, and rather than the usual scuttling around looking for supplies, you cross paths with a merchant ship almost immediately. He welcomes you to the system, noting that you must be a new arrival somehow. He says he's been lucky as well, so he shares a few credits with you as a welcome present before showing you through his products. Gain 5¢. You may trade with a Shop and an Ammo Dealer, both at grade 4.
A: Thank him for his extreme generosity and give him a gift to show your gratitude. Discard one Item or Weapon.
B: Say thank you but leave him without giving him any kind of gift.
9H:
In space, but also on asteroids without atmosphere, you can’t hear people screaming. Or gunﬁ re. Only the sound and the vibration of your own weapon in your hands is recognizable. It is nearly silent, almost peaceful, but it’s a massacre. The others were unarmed and not expecting an attack. All of them are hit and pressed by the force of the impacts against the jet engine of the spaceship.
Like three ghosts they are now start ﬂ oating straight out into space. Then you notice the number imprinted on the ship’s hull. It wasn´t your ship. Confused and starting to panic, you board it to ﬁ nd there are no more humans on board, only a cat with 'MINKA' on their nametag. Even though the cat seems to dislike you, you grab it along with as much of value as you can. Now you really feel like a space pirate. You’re not able to ﬁ nd out who the others were, since the entire onboard computer and all the information on it is encrypted. Gain 5¢ and a 'Laser' Ship System for your Ship.
9I:
You saw mobile traders and ammo dealers, gamblers and many other services and vendors in space, but now for the ﬁ rst time you see a mobile doctor. He has a ﬂ oating medical stretcher and a lot of boxes with wheels following him like little robots.
They offer you a friendly greeting along with a healing and oxygen refuel service.
A: Ask him what his prices are.
B: Threaten him to offer you a one hundred percent discount on his services.
9J: You decide to mute the communication channel with Commander Oona. You can't have reckless wannabe heroes distracting your crew when your own mission is so vital.
9K:
You are greeted by an excited Captain Phoenix.
He tells you that just minutes ago they detected Birdy’s emergency capsule on a dwarf planet. You arrange to meet them at the site and begin your approach immediately.
The meeting on the planet’s surface is a joyful event, until mood drops after the search party discoveres Birdy's empty escape capsule. Then a voice from above calls out to 'Max'. Captain Phoenix looks up along with everyone else to spot Birdy sat high up on a tree, trying to warn you about something. It’s hard to understand the warning, but it quickly becomes clear when the crew comes under attack from ugly creatures in all directions.
Initiate a Ground Combat against: Insectoids, it’s a LV5 Fireﬂ y and two LV4 Exticks as Minions. 'Overland' is the Location (relevant for Treasure drops) / Atmosphere:
Yes. You must succeed in this combat, or you will lose the game. You cannot retreat. You will get Treasures and XP as normal. Continue reading once you have won the combat.
Birdy climbs from his tree and is desperately thankful to you. You notice that he doesn't look too well, ill and out of shape but also oddly quite fat. He's also constantly scratching his belly and seems to be in pain. Melina, their medic, a wise woman with long black hair starts crying, mumbling something like 'not again…' Captain Phoenix silently appears behind Birdy, draws his knife and sinks it into Birdy's neck. It appears to be an instant death. The other ship’s crew runs about 20 meters away. Confused and still in shock, you instinctively follow them.
Melina explains that it was the only good option, to give Birdy peace. On their previous visit to this planet they encountered Exticks. One of their crew fell asleep and was alone for just for a few minutes. They woke to ﬁ nd an Extick near them, which they were able to defeat.
Hours later they looked similar to how Birdy did: ill, bloated, scratching their belly and seemingly in pain. A few hours later that crew member exploded and wounded another crew member nearby. The explosion launched out hundreds of small barbed eggs in all directions, but somehow the crew was fortunate enough that no one else was hit. You will now leave this damned place, leaving Birdy here. Captain Phoenix arranges for a funeral ceremony on board the Titan, using a hologram of Birdy, since they couldn't risk bringing an infection onto the ship.
Sometimes the lessons of this galaxy seem chaotic and illogical, but there is always a lesson to be learned. Gain 20 XP.
9L:
Today you're optimistic about ﬁ nding some information on the Space Kraken as you approach the Renegade base that the information broker gave you the coordinates for. You’re welcomed by a group of well-armed Shadows.
A: You must possess and discard a Medkit to take this option. Offer a gift and ask if they'd be willing to share any information with you.
B: Ask them if they'd be willing to share any information with you.
9M:
It's late at night when you plot your course and leave the planet. As you slump down into your seat and drift off to sleep the board computer wakes you up. A powerless spaceship drifts somewhere off to the right of your ship, nothing to identify it other than an emergency signal. You feel obliged to take a look in case someone needs help. As you approach your heart begins to race as you recognize the ship as that belonging to the Chadwick brothers. Initially there is the fear that they might trap you, but you get a gut feeling that the brothers might not be trapping anyone anymore.
All of your attempts to communicate with the ship fail, but it's clear of radiation so you decide to send a crew over to investigate. 9N:
Arié, who you often forget is a mimic and not actually a human, hails you from a small ﬁ ghter craft and asks if you have some time to spare for a chat and some board games. He mentions having a small collection available.
A: Invite Arié to come onto your ship.
B: Politely turn down the offer and tell him you're too busy.
9P:
At ﬁ rst the spiders begin to crawl around fast and disoriented, but after only a few minutes they shake and then die. Regardless, you wait until one hour has gone by and you're conﬁ dent the gas reached every spot within the ship. Then you wait another hour to get rid of the gas before allowing anyone to take off their space suits. Even then, the ship still stinks like hell.
After a while you feel dizzy. The chemicals cocktail you used seems to have been stronger than predicted and even the microscopic amounts still left in the air are enough to have an effect on you. Following medical inspection the entire crew is slightly weakened for a while.
Until the end of this game turn all ranged Weapon checks made by your crew will be one point more difﬁ cult than usual. This effect expires at the end of this game turn.
9Q:
If the troll did NOT join your Crew, select option B.
You realize the troll is attracted to your Crew Member with the highest Charisma Attribute (if Crew are tied for this, you choose which). Will you allow him to explore that bond, whatever the outcome might be?
A: Yes.
B: Don’t support that bond.
9R:
It's been a while but you ﬁ nd time to visit the Earth colony made by the USS Paraval again. Stefan and Mitchel welcome you but Siegfried doesn't seem to be present.
When you ask about where he is the only answer you get is that his faith was not strong enough and he's gone now, whatever that means. 9U:
You notice hundreds of little spherical objects embedded in the wall to your right. A quick scan detects ash inside, once belonging to living creatures. It seems the spheres are similar to the urns used on Earth. Their shells are made of a rare and valuable alloy.
A: Dump the ashes out and take the alloy shells.
B: Don't touch anything.
9V:
The course is set and nothing stands between you and the secrets hidden within the mysterious wormhole.
Your crew is slightly scared, but you know that to improve your skills and equipment you'll sometimes need to take risks. As for the destination system you have no information other than its coordinates and knowing that it also sits within a Death Sphere. One additional detail is a bit more confusing; the system is said to be a dead system, lacking any life. But then why would it be within a Death Sphere? Maybe because the Mastermind cannot turn it off anymore, or maybe the Mastermind is not the one who controls those Spheres? Maybe for some other strange reason? Anyway, you plan to return back through the wormhole as soon as any danger heads your way.
Right in front of the location where the wormhole should be, you stop and try to locate the gravity anomaly that should give away the wormhole's exact position. Your smartest Crew Member says that if you're close enough, your sensors should be able to detect even the faintest gravitational pull. They also explain that they don't want to ﬁ nd out what happens if your ship comes into contact with the edge of the wormhole. There's a lot that could go wrong, a slight miscalculation in the position of the ship or the wormhole could spell disaster. You correct your position by 5 meters, though at the scale of wormholes it might not even matter. It should be about 3 times the width of your ship and you can't even be sure where you are in relation to it. It seems more like a rabbit hole compared to the giant wormholes that connect this system to Earth. You're not even sure if you'll be able to travel back through the wormhole. Nobody knows for sure if all of them can be passed in two directions and even if so, it’s possible the other side exhibits different forces and features that would make entering from that side too dangerous, if not impossible.
With ﬁ ngers crossed you ﬂ y into it, slowly and carefully.
Seconds later all you can recognize is a tiny white ﬂ ash the edge of your ﬁ eld of vision, a strange feeling, and the as though nothing had occurred you are on the other sid You ﬁ rst note a giant red star that is long into the process of becoming a white dwarf. Even this relatively fast process will take millions of years. The light the star emits is likely only a fraction of its previous intensity, and the single planet that occupies the system bears the scars of the intense heat the red giant once emitted.
You also detect a curious object that seems not to be a planet, despite being larger than the scarred planet.
It has a much darker surface and reﬂ ects waves of all frequencies very poorly, making it hard for your sensors to gather information from it.
You feel like you have entered some vast crypt, disruptin a silence that has lingered for millions of years. The huge structure isn't too far from you and is a safe enough distance from the sun's intense heat, so you plot a course to investigate it with a ﬂ y-by. The distance is still signiﬁ cant enough to justify getting some sleep. As the next simulated morning comes around on your ship, you're woken by the sound of a busy crew at work on the bridge.
The sight of a ship’s hull is visible, though only at the greatest level of telescopic zoom. It seems to be about t size and shape of a planet, teardrop-shaped, gelatinous, a melted structure with an iridescent color that has quit an astonishing appearance... Yet something shatters this beautiful image. What looks like a tattoo on the hull, a mark which has eroded the attractive surface, as if it were an irregular scratch a thousand kilometers deep and stretching across a third of the spaceship. There ar multiple such scratches, like a giant creature attacked t ship and ripped away chunks of its hull with ease.
Nearby you detect what seems to be a docking area on the outside of the hull, various sizes of dock available. Yo choose a suitable one. Once landed, engines cooling dow you set foot upon the ship’s landing platform and can immediately hear very quiet, sad music vibrating throug the hull, through your boots and straight into your head.
A: Explore the monolithic ship.
B: Return to your ship and leave as fast as possible.
9W:
You've spotted a Kraken base, less protected than they usually are. It’s newly built and it's likely they just haven't had time to fortify it yet. This could be a great opportunity to land an easy blow against the Kraken!
A: Try to inﬁ ltrate the base, activate its self-destruct sequence, steal as much of value as you can and then ge out of there!
B: Play it safe and get out of the area.
9X:
The mobile doctor offers the following options. You may choose multiple:

at 4) Spend 11¢ and restore your entire Crew to full HP.
n e. 5) Spend 5¢ and refuel 5 Oxygen.

9Y:
You catch a ﬂ ash of a sailor in a raging storm tying their right hand to the helm, lest they be consumed by the hungry ocean. Then you see yourself sat in your seat, and you fall away from it for an amount of time that could be seconds or months. You feel like you're straining with all your willpower to hold onto something intangible, then there's a surge of light and you're sat in your captain's g chair on board your ship. To your relief you very quickly detect another Earth ship approaching. As it draws near you are surprised to see that its hull has been scarred by what seems to he be years of conﬂ ict, modiﬁ cations and repairs all over, and its weapons and systems seem to largely consist of e technology not found in your ship's database, despite the ship using Earth code identical to your own ship.
“Welcome to the world of the Mastermind, our friends! It's always a pleasure to ﬁ nd more survivors from Earth! We've colonized a small planet in this system and made our home there. You should be aware that there is a Death Sphere here similar u to that which surrounded the Earth, so you'll ﬁ nd many n, species are stranded in this system" they kindly inform you as their ship comes to a stop near your own.
h "But no need to fear, the Space Kraken is ﬁ ghting for us, the Mastermind as they are known here, ﬁ ghting to take control of the system. Please, hear our account of this great being. A: Accept their friendly offer and follow them to their colony.

9Z: You proceed with caution expecting a trap to trigger or some creature to ambush you, but after 5 minutes of collecting the urns and dumping the ashes out, nothing happens. You speed up with the collection as you become more comfortable, though as you leave you still feel uneasy about your decision. Gain 18¢.
A0:
You arrive at the biggest space market again, this time at another location hidden within an asteroid belt. You may trade at a Shop with a grade matching the value noted in line variable A. You may also interact with a Modder and a Gambler. You notice a new spaceship merchant with great prices on ships, and a special offer on as well. It's very rare to see offers this good! A1: She eats the raw meat and asks that next time she gets something really fresh, still warm even. Gain a grade 3 Weapon of your choice.

While retreating from a short and unproductive dungeon exploration, you meet a large alien similar to what you'd consider a troll. Standing 3 meters tall, he's an imposing character, and moves and smells like a bear.
He acts quite friendly as he starts to talk to you through his universal translator. Your initial fear that he might be a threat quickly subsides as you note his warm smile and demeanor. He gets excited about your awesome laser weapon and begs you to sell it to him, but the weapon he's pointing at is actually just a handheld welding laser. You get the impression that behind his strong and friendly exterior, he may not be the most intelligent of beings.

B: Kindly turn him down, explaining that it's not a weapon.

Though hesitant, each of you touches the glowing sphere one after the other, each remaining in contact with the A.I. it contains before stepping away with a very odd expression.
For each of your Crew Members except your Leader may now do one of the following; - Increase one Attribute by up to 2 points (max 8).
- Remove a Trait.
- Gain a Trait.
Assuming you all survive the resulting headache, this might prove to be one of your most productive missions so far! You navigate your way back out of the gigantic craft with ease, the entirety of its seemingly endless ﬂ oor plan somehow clear in your mind, before boarding your ship and heading back out through the wormhole. Weary from your experience, you drift into a slumber. You wake to ﬁ nd the entire crew asleep, though luckily your ship is on standby having successfully completed the journey back through the wormhole under autopilot.

As you open the door you have to refrain from laughing at the sight you're presented with. Before you stand two aliens, humanoid bodies, but their heads are very clearly ﬁ sh bowls ﬁ lled with water, and inside each a ﬁ sh looking, as ﬁ sh tend to, rather expressionless. The way they're standing suggests they're not overly well balanced. “Please help us! We are Namnum and Numnam, after we passed through that horrifying wormhole, our colony ship accidentally rushed off without us. Please take us to the next exit! We'll give you all of our cash, 30,000 piscis if you can help us."
A: Help them.
B: Slowly close the door without speaking.
A5:
You check your ammo and injuries before heading through a gigantic bulkhead and into a vast spherical vault so large you can't see the other side. Down its center runs a seemingly endless gangway, resting on the bottom of a deep blue body of water that obscures the entire vault. You're able withstand the extreme pressure in the vault by hacking into the mobile shield that covers the bulkhead area. Using this shield you're able to make your way towards the center of the vault. There are guards in specialized suits that attempt to attack you, but with the shield's power coming directly from the power core, they aren't even able to cause it to ﬂ icker. They begin a counter-hack but you should have a decent amount of time before they get through.
At the center of the vault you ﬁ nd a terminal detailing the functions and parameters of the power source, revealing that this entire planet is a gigantic fusion reactor.
Somewhere ahead of you in the vault's chasm there is an entire star burning. Whether it's real or artiﬁ cial you can't tell, but according to the readings, its energy output is astronomical. Strangely the terminal displays only a single output, the planetary shield, which seems to be consuming just 1% of the star's output. The other 99% is being sent through what you suspect is some sort of inter-dimensional relay, sending the energy to some unfathomable device that then projects a Death Sphere into this dimension.
Regardless of this, your options seem pretty limited. If you power down the reactor or destroy it, the internal shields will deactivate, along with the containment shields around the star. You have no idea how the star ever fueled its own containment facility to begin with, but shutting it off now would cause the entire planet to detonate. You certainly can't retreat now, since the shield holding the pressure back is likely to fail before you make it back to the vault entrance. There's some mention of a teleporter on the console, though the technology is unfamiliar and you're not sure how it might work. It seems like your only option at this point.
Combine the Tech Attribute of your entire Crew and add two d6 rolls to the result. This result will indicate which Event you read next;
A: If the result is 3-17.
B: If the result is 18 or above.

You charge through the base taking down a number of smaller Kraken before they're able to retaliate. You're able to avoid contact with any armed guards, but your crew takes a beating from a number of sentry turrets you run into. Fortunately your efforts pay off as you discover a room full of alien research equipment, at its center a device that looks older than the universe itself. It seems to be the reason behind this newly constructed Kraken research facility. You take it.
Distribute 10 points of damage among your Crew Members however you wish, ignoring Armor and Shields (if none of your Crew Members have HP left, your Campaign has failed and ends here.
Increase the Line’s variable E by +1.
Gain one of the following Weapons:
'Arc riﬂ e (7) RG 4+, 10 T2 AP, A4'. You cannot sell it or buy Ammo for this. After the end of each Game Turn (not combat turn) this Weapon is reloaded automatically.
'Arc pistol (5) RG 4+, 8 T2 AP, A3'. You cannot sell it or buy Ammo for this. After the end of each Game Turn (not combat turn) this Weapon is reloaded automatically.
A8:
While burning time watching an old TV series during a long space ﬂ ight you receive a message. It's a bounty posting for one of your crew members, speciﬁ cally dead, a 50¢ reward upon delivery. You try to stay calm. You mull around the ship a little while and it seems that you were the only one to receive the message. Then you start to think about your situation... Choose an option:

Lure your chosen crew member into the med bay for a 'routine drugs test' and administer a tranquilizer to put them to sleep. B: Ignore the request. You would never betray one of your crew members!
A9:
You decide to follow them despite the difﬁ culty of remaining undetected as you do so. Your Leader makes an Agility Check against 7+.
A: Read this Event if you pass the check.
B: Read this Event if you fail the check.
AA:
You meet a mobile trader in the middle of nowhere.
You may trade at a Shop with a grade matching the value in Line Variable A. You may also make a single Charisma Check against 8+ with a Crew Member of your choice. If they pass you can increase the Shop's grade by 1.
AB:
Tracking down the Kraken ships that destroyed the small station, you're able to ﬁ nd them at a slave camp and soon come up with a plan for rescuing the captives there. Your plan has a few vital ingredients; a few spoons of surprise, a dash of your ship's heavy weapons and most importantly, a spicy (and highly combustible) tanker to break down the prison wall. You suspect getting the tanker will be the hardest part, but by pure luck you come across one undergoing repairs at a nearby service point and you're certain not to let this chance slip by.
You let the repair crew ﬁ nish their work and then blast their vessel before taking control of the tanker. There will no doubt be a distress signal alerting the nearby Kraken forces, but your mission will be done before they can properly mobilize. It gets a little messy when you have to 'procure' the driver's tentacle to use as a genetic key to gain control, but other than that it's a clean process.
Without delay you establish remote control over the tanker, make your way back to your ship and send it towards the wall of the slave camp. It's an impressively effective solution. The tanker weathers a small amount of panicked defensive ﬁ re before it strikes the boundary wall and explodes with great force, knocking out the shields, most of the turrets and a number of guards on the inside.
You can't afford to lose the element of surprise and so charge forward, deploying directly into the breach where you ﬁ nd a number of Kraken guards ready for a ﬁ ght.
Initiate a Ground Combat LV4 Enemy encounter, (L.Diff.
Already included), 6th Map of Space Station as spawning and Treasure parameter / Atmosphere: Yes / Species:
Kraken. Apply the Ambush effect. You must succeed in this combat, or you will lose the game. You cannot retreat. You will get Treasures and XP as normal for this combat.
AC: The two ﬁ shbowl heads tell you they're so grateful, though their expressions remain unchanged, as is normal for ﬁ sh. As you advance you realize just how incapable the two aliens are as they wobble around and generally struggle with simple tasks. You have to commit one of your crew entirely to assisting them. AD:
You watch the strangers. The ship isn't yours, though you recognize the number printed on it. They must have been forced to land on the other side of the asteroid by something and it appears there's some damage to their engines. You greet them using a light-based short range transmission to avoid drawing any unwanted attention.
Minutes later you shake hands and they invite you into their ship for a cup of coffee.
There are three of them: Rhenaya, Segallion and Loewenherz, German astronauts and scientists, along with their cat Minka that they smuggled away with them when they left Earth. The cat seems to appreciate the company of your crew and you're glad to see some other human faces as well. You tell them your story and they tell you theirs. They claim to have been in this system for a couple of years now, despite that by their recollection, their ship only left Earth a few days before yours did.
Their plan is to develop a transmitter that can produce signals able to neutralize, possibly even control Kraken.
They speak of a DNA sequence installed into the original Kraken before releasing it into the sea, but somehow this sequence seems to have altered or deactivated. The smaller Kraken that serve under the Mastermind have developed differently however, and the DNA sequence is still alive, possibly even enhanced, and there's a good chance it is playing some role in how the Mastermind is able to control its Kraken servants. The scientists were in the process of testing the transmitter on a small Kraken scout ship when they were detected and came under ﬁ re.
They managed to get away despite taking damage to their engine, crash landing at this location where their ship is currently immobilized. They ask if you could take them with you and since they're unlikely to survive by themselves, you agree. They aren't trained or experienced in combat, so they agree to remain on your ship and stay out of any tense situations. Instead, they will continue to work on their device in the hopes of discovering a weapon able to control the Kraken. They predict that the completion of the device will eventually require 25¢, and would be grateful if you could provide this funding in the near future. They decide to trust you with the funding an give you what credits they have stashed. Gain 10¢.
AE:
You encounter a mobile trader in the middle of nowhere. Trading seems to be one of the most common jobs in this system, even more than piracy. You again encounter t he troll who is glad to see you. He considers you his greatest friend and recalls how helpful you are every time he meets you. He suggests th it would be great if he could join your crew!

You are able to reach them within 30 minutes, docking and boarding as soon as you arrive. Heavy gunﬁ prevents you from safely moving forward, forcing you to engage the enemy.
