Kraken. You must succeed in this combat, or you will los the game. You cannot retreat. You will get Treasures and XP as normal.
AI: You leave the dead system as fast as you can, the wormhole spitting you out exactly where you started you journey. Space exploration is not for the faint of heart!
AJ:
Your navigation system blares out one alarm after another as you drift among a ﬁ eld of debris from what looks like a recent battle, having chosen a more dangerous route in an effort to avoid a nearby Kraken d patrol. Your crew works to maintain shield integrity whilst the long range sensors alert you to a number of different ships nearby. Make an Agility check against 8+ with your Leader.
A: Read this Event if you pass the check.
B: Read this Event if you fail the check.
a
AK:
A mobile ammo dealer greets you, glad to meet someone after accidentally stumbling on this location. You may trade with an Ammo dealer at a grade equal to the value in Line Value A.
m f
AL: After possibly setting a new record in rapid repairs your crew manages to get the ventilation system working again by removing about one hundred and twenty happy squeaking ﬂ uffy rainbow colored little creatures from the suction’s intake. They are also found in nearly every section of the ventilation system. With all those sweet pet-like creatures the race against death somehow becomes quite exciting and fun. Sadly, the process takes too long and before you are able to restore function to the ﬁ rst engine you hear a terrifying crash. The corridor to the machine room has collapsed entirely. It seems leaving the creatures to breed within the ship without monitoring them may have been a mistake. At least the end is fast as the bridge and remainder of the ship collapses in on itself a second later. Your Campaign has failed and ends here.
AM:
During another fruitless exploration near where you last met the troll, you ﬁ nd yourself questioning whose idea at it was to search this place for items and weapons again when your ship relays a message to you.
“Hey friends, hope to see you soon! Here's a present from your old pal Masa!"
s The software attached to the message automatically installs itself to your space suit, a threat detection early warning system. Make a note: When you begin your next Ground Combat, read Event 'CO'.
re You soon come across the friendly troll again. He looks as if he's had a tough time. Despite some clear wounds, he's still as enthusiastic as ever about once again meeting his best friends. He tells you he has found an old yellow helmet with two green and white racing stripes on top, nearly big enough to wear, and he plans to use it to e explore some unmapped territories that seem to have a toxic atmosphere. Without prompting he throws some credits your way and asks you if you have some tip or item to help him.
.
A: Grab some duct tape from one of your packs, write some made up advice on it and wish him good luck as you hand it to him. Gain 5¢.
d B: Return the credits and explain that the helmet won't protect him against a toxic atmosphere.
AN: You leave the Kraken base behind. Whatever is going on there, you don't want to get involved.
AO:
You receive a message from the Greys and decide r to read it in secret, knowing what kind of business the Greys are often involved in. They want to buy one of your crew members (the one lowest on your Crew Sheet) but decline to give a reason why. They mention an abandoned space station where they'll meet you to make the trade.
Their offer is 200¢. Will you accept the deal?
A: You will never betray your Crew! Decline their offer.
B: You may only choose this if you have more than one Crew Member. Yes... two hundred credits can save a lot more than one life. You'll have to try and keep this a secret though, the crew probably aren't going to like being sold off.
AP: You ﬁ nd three friendly ships, an ammo dealer, a gambler and a modder all docked together. They welcome your company and politely try and encourage you to invest in their goods and services. You may trade with an Ammo Dealer, Gambler and Modder all at grade 6.
AQ: It seems it was a good decision to hurry. One of the Kraken ﬂ eets sent around 100 small and a dozen heavier ships. No doubt such a vast ﬂ eet will ﬁ nd you eventually, but for now you should prioritize improving your ship and crew to give yourself a ﬁ ghting chance when that day comes. A lot of strange different species seem to be living here, trading and functioning in concealment. If they can survive under these conditions, so can you.
AR:
During a quiet spell you're amazed that you're able to ﬁ nd what seems to be an underground virtual network, something similar to Earth's 'dark web', and it's populated with intriguing and exciting projects to support. One speciﬁ c project draws your attention. A heavily armored spaceship, delivered directly to you for just 25¢. There's a note stating that the ship comes pre-assembled but unpainted, which seems like an odd thing to specify, but you don't fully understand the cultural norms around here.
The offer says that it's only open for another 20 minutes!
You note there's a local merchant you can just about reach if you need to balance your credits out. You may sell Equipment as you would at a Shop before choosing an option. You can't buy anything there.
A: Buy it! Pay 25¢.
B: Stick with your current ship.
AS: It seems everything does have a price. Even if they were surprised by your conditions in the beginning, they accept them. They hand over the weapon, wishing you luck as they leave. Gain a Mejang 'Gauss riﬂ e' (see Weapons list, grade 3)
AU:
You give them a few days to develop a deeper friendship. You Crew Member with the highest Charisma Attribute (you choose if tied) must make a Charisma Check.
On a 9+ you can choose one of the troll's Attributes to increase by 1, ignoring all max Attribute limits.
On a 12+ you must instead erase the Crew Member that made the check. You may keep their Inventory. You may choose to keep or erase the troll Crew Member. The troll was so fond of them it devoured them in the night.
AV:
After defeating the Kraken guards you spare no time in releasing the slaves held captive in the camp.
Many of them will remember your face as the hero who saved them. You're relieved when you spot Arié among the captives and pull him onto your ship. He's grateful to see you and is quick to share the secret codes that will allow you to contact Commander Oona, having stored them only in his memory, which is quite impressive considering the code is over 30 digits long!
He tells you of how he'd become certain they were all going to die eventually. He mentions that some prisoners were set to be traded as food at a solar station, so you suspect there wouldn't be a return journey. You drop Arié off at the next station and as you depart he promises to ﬁ nd the location of Commander Oona and report back to you. He's even more eager to get revenge on the Kraken now. As you depart your ship's sensors ﬁ nish their analysis of the slave facility and the Kraken forces inside, using them to improve your crew training program and equipment. Gain 20 XP.
AW: You teleport right onto the Chadwicks’ spaceship and try to ﬁ re wildly at the equipment to draw some attention. The weapons don't function at all, a red light glowing on their displays, and before you have a new plan you are plucked up by servant robots like ripe fruit from a tree, and brought before the Chadwicks. The robots use you as a punchbag for a good minute, delivering several punches before teleporting you back to your ship and keeping the weapons. The Chadwicks’ ship disappears in space. Erase all the Chadwick's Weapons from your characters and ships Inventory
AX: You have bigger priorities right now, you'll no doubt ﬁ nd your answers over time anyway. Better keep on moving.
AY:
You agree to join Guzz on their ship and hear their tale. "Wonderful! I'll send a shuttle over to fetch you."
From the underside of the enormous head a small shuttle emerges, also insect-like in its appearance, even possessing small buzzing wings in spite of the lack of atmosphere. Upon arrival you inspect the shuttle, noting again that there's a complete lack of weapon systems, and that the interior looks quite spacious and comfortable.
You enter and soon the shuttle is taking you over to Guzz's ship.
You are greeted by very strange but oddly luxurious surroundings. The insectoid appearance of the exterior is replaced by strange pinkish ﬂ owing shapes, very organic, no straight lines in sight. The ﬂ oor is a soft spongy rubbery surface which is surprisingly easy to walk on, as though it is adjusting to support your weight as you move.
"Please, sit" comes the voice of Guzz. You look around, but see no-one. You take a seat in one of the pink hammocks and wait for your host.
"Greetings travelers, it has been so long since I had anyone to talk with!" comes Guzz's voice again, "I have traveled for millennia and had many companions over that time, but alas their lives are only ﬂ eeting moments in a life as long as mine, and my own kind are long gone."
You become increasingly curious as to the nature of this being, exploring the room with your eyes. It has a very much biological nature to it, warm colors, and is oddly humid. As you look closer, the hammocks appear to be a membrane stretched over what looks like bone structures. You panic as you begin to suspect that you are actually inside a living creature.
"Easy my child." says Guzz , "Should I have wished you dead, you would already have suffered such a fate.
My words are honest, I simply wish to speak." As you calm down and try to put the organic nature of your surroundings to the back of your mind, Guzz is true to their word and tells you many stories about their adventures in this universe and another place, the Light Universe. Tales of self-replicating evil robot armies and friendly undead assassins carry you both deep into the night.
Guzz asks for your story, and you return the favor, telling them of your adventures escaping from Earth and your pursuit of the Space Kraken. You mention that Guzz's assistance would be a big help, but they kindly decline, stating that they are merely an observer and must not interfere. Guzz does offer one piece of advice before they depart.
"Remember, just because something looks big and bad does not mean it is your enemy." The clue seems ominous, and your mind wonders again as to what exactly Guzz is.
You wish them good luck on their travels and head back to your ship, having learned a lot from Guzz's stories. Gain 12 XP.
AZ: For a second there's a horrible feeling, like you're about to fall down a great bottomless hole designed to destroy the soul, or no, maybe replace it with something hollow. Before any other distracting thoughts pop into your head you use the cleanser to collect the substance from your glove and neutralize the entire solution, every drop. Once the machine is done you carefully dump the entire crate out the trash shoot and try to forget it ever existed.
B0:
Rhenaya and the other two scientists let you know that they are ready to build the transmitter. They predict that the device could produce a range of effects, from disorientating Krakens to disrupting the control network that commands them, or potentially even directly enabling control over them. They'll need high power transmitting equipment, which they know how to obtain, but they need your help covering the cost of purchasing the equipment.
A: Save your Credits for something more important.
The scientists will have to make do with spare parts and whatever they can scavenge.
B: Invest in their project to ensure they have the greatest odds of success. Pay 25¢.
B1:
You're annoyed to ﬁ nd a message from Masa: "Can't wait to meet up! I've sent you a pod with some of my stuffed Artopian rabbits, I know you'll love these!" You ponder what the hell an Artopian rabbit is and why you'd want a stuffed one. Your pondering is disturbed by a deafening bang that shakes the entire ship. It seems to be Masa's pod, the contents destroyed along with a section of your ship's hull. You feel a growing sense of hatred for this guy!
Note that during the Next Space Combat within this game turn, your Hull SP will be 2 lower.
B2:
Dr. Leigh freezes abruptly and stares at you for an endless moment. Then his expression very slightly saddens as he states with glossed eyes; “Oh ok, I understand, it's OK. I had assumed it was normal among Homo sapiens, or what was it, humans? I once knew a stranded human and he seemed to love such greetings.
But never mind, let us talk business.”
B3: You meet the friendly troll again. He's alive and in better shape than last time, no sign of the helmet anywhere. Somehow, he still thinks you are his best friends, despite that the laser 'weapon' you sold him would have been basically useless. He tells you he must leave this place to go back to his tribe, leaving you with an item he doesn't seem to be able to operate himself. You gain a Heavy Energy Shield (Grade 3 Item).
B4: You decline the Greys’ offer, their response a maniacal, evil laughter, before telling you that they have been watching you since you arrived in the system. They will hunt and kill all of you anyway! Then they end the transmission.
B5:
Your long-range sensors spot something following you a few times, but if you try to scan it, it disappears.
Space travel is unavoidable; if you're going to continue on your mission, you consider how important it is to keep improving your ship, since you never know when you might come up against a tough situation.
B6:
It feels like the shape of your mind is being warped, crushed by a cramped container that it doesn't ﬁ t into, tightening with each passing moment. The A.I. warns you again of the danger you are exposing yourself to. In the following minutes you gain more knowledge than years of committed study could provide. Somewhere among the storm of information you feel what must be blood running from your nose. You even feel the ﬂ ow of knowledge now, almost like you can reach out and shape it like clay. Gain a new Trait, or increase your Tech, Agility, R anged or Melee Attribute by 2, ignoring maximum Attribute limits.
Your Leader takes d6 damage, ignoring Shields and Armor. The leader can only drop to 1HP minimum from this effect.
Despite all the knowledge yo u have gained, you cannot tell how much more of this process you will be able to survive.
You note that oddly you are not as scared for your life as you probably should be, but that instead you are making a calculated, logical decision in weighing the risks and rewards of continuing the transfer.
A: Continue with the process.
B: End the session.
B7: You catch mention of a breach at a nearby Kraken slavery station, the prisoners managing to overwhelm the guards and escape. Only a small number of the slaves survived the massacre and you wonder if Arié was among the survivors...
B8:
You enter the Chadwick brothers' ship using your small shuttle. An atmosphere of doom and dread accompany a smell of sulfur, reminding you of the brothers. The teleportation system is somehow jammed, and some sensors show weird readings. It is a small comfort that there's no radiation here and the atmosphere is breathable. You search for the crew, and it doesn’t take long to ﬁ nd the command bridge, and the brothers. Both are dead, looking like they'd had their souls scared from their bodies, mouths and eyes wide open, still sat in their chairs. Your medic tries to analyze their bodies when suddenly you hear a deep voice. Right in front of you, as if it was always there, a humanoid creature stands. The voice is warm, like that of one who likes a glass of wine in the evening, but also distinctly inhuman, sinister and evil.
You remember stories you heard on the planet you recently visited, tales of a reaper who feeds on souls an was banished somehow. It sounded like some nonsense for spooking kids around a campﬁ re late at night, but no the nightmare is much more convincing.
“I would thank you for releasing me from my 3 thousand years of imprisonment, but this meal you serve is the blandest and most rubbery I've ever known. No contrast in ﬂ avors between the two dishes. Mortal beings who thought they could make a self-serving deal with one such as me. I grant wishes to those who pray to me, thei energy fueling my escape from my prison. Where did you think they got those weapons, ammo appearing from nowhere? And in their greed they took my prison from a place I could have never escaped. And you my friend, it took barely half an hour for you to break it entirely. Of course, I must thank you properly for this next course you have brought to me. Their souls look to be ripe and nutritious.”
Initiate a Ground Combat against a Soul Reaper (creatures from hell), Space Station as spawning and Treasure parameter / Atmosphere: Yes. Roll for the initiative as usual. You cannot retreat from this combat.
You will get Treasures and XP as normal. Use only the Crew you chose in the previous Event '9M' for this combat. The Crew Members you left on your ship are not involved and are safe even if you lose this combat.
B9:
The surface of the planet looks like a moon, nothing but dust and rocks. The only reason to land here would b to hide for maintenance, maybe even setup a little base for a while, far away from the Kraken, pirates and all the other threats. You approach a deep crater to ﬁ nd some cover, but to your surprise it turns out to be a huge tunn leading deep into the planet. Inexplicably large, you're on edge as you travel through the tunnel, certain that at an moment a giant worm will emerge and obliterate your sh without even noticing it was there. You try to push image of cheap Earth Sci-Fi movies out of your mind.
The tunnel seems to expand in places and is smaller aga in others, different offshoots splitting and rejoining. Afte a half hour ﬂ ight you land at what seems to be the end of the tunnel, approximately 100km beneath the surface of the planet. There’s a breathable atmosphere here, despite your incredible depth, and no worms in sight.
Your disbelief fades as you slowly convince yourself that it might actually be safe to leave the ship and explore on foot.
A horizontal tunnel around half the size of your ship lead you north, a feature apparently drilled out with handheld machines. It leads you to a place unlike any you've seen before. A giant cavity higher and wider than your eyes ca behold. The air is warm, some form of palm tree growing in abundance, the land illuminated by a static source of light sat at the very top of the vast cavern. There are also vast areas of cultivated farmland. The impressive and peacefully dreamlike scenery is quickly marred as shots from energy weapons sear across the environmen Palms burst into ﬂ ames and chunks of Earth are thrown into the air. You jump into a deep water trench to take cover. Odd-colored humanoids ﬁ ght against armed humanoid insects. You don't seem to be of any interest t either side, and the insects don't seem to notice you at a After dozens of soldiers fall on both sides the insectoid forces retreat and you are surrounded by the humanoid species. Big black eyes examine you closely. They look d like humans, but their skin is of two colors. It is a mix of ebony and ivory with silver shining at their neck, their w bodies mostly the brighter color, with only the hands, feet and head adorning the darker color. Their hair is silvery white. Their faces and ﬁ gures seem to vary in the same way human faces tend to. They look friendly and seem surprised to see you, introducing you to this place they call Aeus, a perfect world created by their species, the Mejang. At least they seem to believe it would be perfect if it wasn't for the plague of beings they refer r to as the Morrocks, who they've been in conﬂ ict with for many generations. Their war pre-dates the arrival of the Mastermind, whose presence is of little interest to them.
They are aware of the threat the Mastermind poses to all living things, but they are focused on their own struggles at the moment. You assure them that you'll conceal the existence of their species from the outside and are looking for a place to hide yourself. They seem convinced by your story.
They make it clear that they wish to end their war with the Morrocks soon, no matter the price, and ask for your help. They want you to spy on the Morrocks for them. The Morrocks also avoid the outside world, though they are not hostile towards visitors. You should be able to easily involve yourself in their society and gather information on what plans they are making.
A: Agree to help end the war by spying on the Morrocks.
B: Agree to spy on the Morrocks, but demand some of the e Mejangs' weapons as up-front payment.
BA:
As the last of the Mastermind's guards falls lifeless to the ground you check your equipment before heading el through the bulkhead leading to the bridge. You enter a giant hall, its grand size not half as intimidating as the y gigantic ﬁ gure stood calmly at its center, its gaze ﬁ xed on ip you like a statue. You feel the intense burn of an electric s fear as you behold what must surely be the Mastermind itself. Surprisingly it looks nothing like a Kraken beyond its great size, being something as much machine as organic, in a twisted dance of ﬂ esh and synthetic materials.
r It opens its mouth for what you suspect will be some grand speech explaining its twisted ambitions, but as you calm down, the memories of all the suffering it has caused conjures a rage inside your mind. Before it can speak you decide to try and catch it off guard, shooting directly at its face. The Mastermind's brains explode out of its skull before they can even speak a word, their body falling into a lump and a silence coming to rest over the room. Only s a beeping sound can be heard coming from a neural chip lying on the ground near some of the chunks of strange looking brain matter. A number of Kraken guards and n servants in the room seem to become confused, beginning to crawl around in circles and apparently no longer aware of your presence.
After the shock of what just happened fades you inspect the neural chip and ﬁ nd that it attaches automatically t. to your skull and is capable of controlling a number of things, including the Flagship you're on. More importantly, it can control the Death Spheres and a highly advanced teleporter / wormhole generator ﬁ tted to the ship. You o don't understand how it works at all, though it seems ll.
receptive to your input. The teleporter is capable of long distance teleportation, far enough to reach Earth, and it also grants you access to the Mastermind's extensive database of technologies and scientiﬁ c discoveries that will without doubt help Earth overcome many of the problems it once faced. You deactivate the Death Sphere without needing to think about it, for whoever and whatever might be trapped by it, you are also its prisoner.
Now you must consider how to approach returning to Earth;
A: Immediately attempt to return to Earth. Though you're not sure how the teleporter works, it might also only be active for a limited time before some aspect of it expires or shuts off, and you might not be able to re-activate it again without a command from the recently very dead Mastermind.
B: If Earth still exists it can wait another day or two, and the distance you're aiming to travel is immense. Take some time to learn about the Mastermind's ship and the long-range teleporter so that you can hopefully avoid any serious mistakes.
BB:
First you lost items, then you lost a Kraken-like pet, followed by a crew member. Now some bizarre state of mind overcomes you as the whole Crew seems to become alien to you, no doubt partly a result of their cold attitude towards you over the past few days. You walk to a local market to buy some supplies, but upon your return you ﬁ nd your ship is gone and your crew are nowhere in sight. You feel alone and hopeless. You drop down onto the scorched vegetation where the ship had previously landed. Hours seem to pass.
A: You can't give up on your mission. You've found a ship you could steal, coincidentally a similar model to your previous one. Erase all Equipment in your Ship Storage.
Erase all Crew other than your Leader.
B: Head deep into the forest on foot.
BC:
You receive another transmission from Adam, encrypted, but only with standard methods used on Earth which you're easily able to decode.
Adam, transmission #2:
“Maybe it is only the rage I hold within me that makes the current agony of my existence bearable. I hide, like a rat in rubble. Every night I have the same nightmare:
creatures looming over me taking samples from my body while I suffer, longing for death. Yet, these very same nightmares seem to force me to live through my imprisonment and torture again and again. You have no idea what evil power pulls these strings. When Earth's wormhole spat me out here, I wanted to crash Max's ship on a planet with low gravity, hoping to somehow survive just long enough to give him a decent traditional burial.
Please forgive me Max.
Before I could even prepare a basic plan, the Mastermind found me. I was surrounded by an entire ﬂ eet of dark black ships that cannot be compared to anything built by humanity. As they intercepted me, all I could do was catapult Max into space and hope that they would only capture me and the ship. I remember that the space around me crackled as the worst electric shock imaginable shot through me. I woke up in a tiny cell, 6 bare walls of dark steel. As a refugee from Earth, I was probably exotic enough to them to attract attention. It came to examine me, while its minions were getting me ready for some sort of dissection in what I recall as being a gigantic room.
Imagine an autopsy being performed on you, only without being dead, and with never-ending rounds of agonizing pain. They cut out of me what they found interesting, then they healed me only to cut me open again at another place. I could sense the formation of schemes being designed by this huge, grotesquely formed body working from behind thick shatterproof glass, behind the reﬂ ection of tentacles, eyes I will never forget. No... not the eyes, but the dark energy that lingered within them. A hatred and contempt belonging to a creature so insanely evil.
Finally, I escaped! Living in the ruins of lost worlds, as I was fueled by dreams of paying that vile being back, though at ﬁ rst, I couldn't even build the most basic ship out of scrap. But I'm working on it.
Do not seek me at my current location, this message will not be transmitted until I have left this planet. I have one small piece of advice for you. The Mastermind has as many names as there are stars; sometimes he is identiﬁ ed as the Shadow, at other times one of a thousand other variations. If people speak of this evil by one of these names, you will always know by a particular terror in their eyes and voices that they are indeed referring to this very same evil Mastermind I am telling you about.
The fear runs deep, even for those who were never in its captivity. The most often-used names seem to be '4P669' and a word that its Kraken servants use, usually spoken by the universal translator as 'Mastermind'.
Be on your guard!
Adam.”
BD:
After a one-hour ﬂ ight you land at the abandoned space station and immediately start to doubt whether this was a good idea, something about the scenery making you very uneasy. Maybe it's just that your crew doesn't know the true nature of your visit. You don't have to put them off for long as the Greys appear from two sides and before you are able to start talking, they start ﬁ ring.
The crew panics and scrambles back to the ship. With the Greys approaching the ship is launched without hesitation, safely escaping the hostile forces. Then one crew member points out that someone is missing. Erase your Leader and their Equipment, then appoint a new Leader.
BE:
After record fast repairs your crew manages to get the ventilation system working again by removing about ﬁ fty happy squeaking furry rainbow colored little creatures from the intake vent. They are also in nearly every other section of the ventilation system. With all those sweet pet-like creatures the race against death is strangely fun. Then you focus on repairing the engines.
You hear the sound of wrenching metal as part of the ship collapses, but you don't have time to check what it is.
Then with a loud “yehaaaaaa!” the engine comes to life again, like it was a great bull that some rodeo rider had just leaped onto. Just a few seconds before your ship crashes and is obliterated you're able to regain control and begin gaining altitude. Sadly you lose three of the ship's crew, poor souls, so full of hope and joy. Maybe it was four, or even ﬁ ve? Despite that they nearly killed your entire crew, you can't be angry at the little chirpy ﬂ uffballs. Somehow you need to limit their living space inside the ship and control their population. Certainly their presence is likely to liven up any future journeys.
One crew member even tries to name them all after realizing each of them has a unique color pattern to their fur. A damage report reveals that excessive atmospheric pressure has caused damage to some parts of the ship, but overall the vessel is stable. Erase one existing Ship System from your sheet.
As part of your population control measures you're able to justify selling about half of the ﬂ uffy creatures at the gas planet's station, though there's still sadness to selling them off. Gain 5 XP and 13¢.
BF:
Despite the chaos you spot the barely visible silhouette of a space station hiding inside a hollow asteroid nearby. You’ve seen this fast-spinning shape twice before. It’s the biggest space market! You decide this could be a good time to pay it a visit whilst you wait for the chaos to die down. Again you see the spaceship merchant and he offers you a special 'new for old' deal.
You may trade at a Shop with a grade matching the value noted in line variable A. You may also interact with a Modder and a Gambler. You may buy any Spaceship you want at a 25¢ discount! The full purchase price of your current ship is also discounted from the cost of the new ship (you cannot gain Credits this way).
You pretty quickly piece together why his prices are so good when he offers to take slaves as payment, and you have to try and keep yourself calm. He's eager to remind you that this is a one-time offer, only available right here and now. You may sell any of your Crew Members and gain 15¢ for each one sold. Sold Crew Members are erased, but you may keep their inventories.
BG:
At a small market you browse through a volume of useless junk and eventually ﬁ nd a yellow helmet! It has one white and two green stripes on it and inside you can barely read the letters KE?N. You can’t read the third letter. The entire surface looks like it has been eroded by acid, little pieces of duct tape still visible. All the merchant knows is that the previous owner was found dead, so it's unlikely anyone is going to come looking for the helmet.
With a bad feeling, you leave the market.
BH:
Are you really sure you want to use the airlock to dump Masa into space?
A: Yes, he deserves it. Open the airlock!
B: He is a sentient living being and dumping him into the void of space is something which violates moral and intergalactic law (if this twisted region of space has such things). But he still deserves it. Open the airlock!
BI:
You enter the giant ship through a massive bulkhead which you open by simply pressing a holographic switch.
As you exit the airlock you check the atmosphere, opening your helmet to take a deep breath. It smells old and strange somehow. There’s no sign of life, no aliens or plants or even the most minute insect. The only evidence is the empty space suits which are placed on the wall. The suits look interesting.
A: Try one of the suits on.
B: Don't try a suit on.
BJ:
Back at the ocean planet with the submerged trader you ﬁ nd a jungle market on the surface where wild looking creatures are dealing in energy crystals. Hidden tunnels and the strong energy signatures make a complete scan of the place impossible. Do you want to head down and explore the trading options there?
A: Yes, carefully.
B: Better avoid this place and continue your ﬂ ight.
BK:
Even though Adam left, you visit the planet that he sent the message from. Its red atmosphere has a rotten smell and the surface looks like an endless garbage dump. There are no signs of Adam. There’s only a small transmitter set to automatically broadcast his message over and over.
Hidden under the ruins of an old mining station you ﬁ nd a secret trader ship buried inexplicably deep down. They welcome you and seem keenly interested in humans, possibly regarding them as an exotic species given how out of the way they are. A Trader greets you, introducing themselves as Aaaron (with 3 A's). They show off a number of strange little games they've created in that dark, gloomy workshop, but when you look at the prices you see that they are all labeled 'not for sale'. You decide to check out the normal stock. You may Trade with a grade 3 Shop. Choose a Crew Member and make a Charisma Check against 7+. If you pass the Charisma check, each Item or Weapon you buy from this Shop costs 1¢ less.
BL:
A diabolo shaped spaceship appro aches you and establishes video contact, conﬁ dently fat, ugly creatures that look like naked bears introducing themselves as the Bayjuy. Seeming to be quite simple minded individuals, they ask if you are selling your hand weapons and offer to pay full price for them. Without warning they teleport straight onto your ship, but before you respond they're already laughing and exploring like curious, friendly children. You may sell any of your Weapons at full price.
One asks eagerly if they can 'play' with one of your hand weapons, which you optimistically assume is the universal translator doing its best with their primitive language. Before you realize what’s going on one of them is holding a weapon and posing like an action hero, before accidentally ﬁ ring a shot into their companion's foot.
Half of your crew prepare for combat, weapons ready in seconds, but the Bayjuy are just laughing and mocking their crewmate who is now hopping around holding their foot. Despite their unsettling appearance, their presence isn't unpleasant. They seem to take things well. Quite a while passes before they say their goodbyes and leave your ship, still laughing and talking about how interesting it was, and making plans to ﬁ nd you again in the future so they can trade with you. DR:
“Oh, I see" he whispers in disappointment. “Was the railgun not to your satisfaction? Was it faulty?
You have had so much time to do this small favor for me. Never mind, it's in the past. What matters now is that we understand each other, understand how these occurrences make us feel. I'd like to clarify how I feel, since it seems I wasn't clear during your last visit.” Dr.
Leigh opens his mouth to what you suspect is its full width, the ﬂ esh of his face stretching so far that you wouldn't even know it was a face anymore. A tunnel into hell, black and endless, walls coated in an incoherent assortment of razor sharp teeth.
His tongue rolls out slowly like a red carpet. Expecting a ﬁ ght, your crew raises weapons, though Leigh remains motionless a few meters in front of you. Then one of your crew steps forward. It looks like they're going to attempt to negotiate for some reason. They come to a stop right before Dr. Leigh's tongue and after an ominous pause turn with apparent difﬁ culty to face you, tears running from their eyes as they ﬁ ght against their own emotions.
Then their expression falls plain and they turn back before walking straight into the gruesome maw.
In a panic you attempt to open ﬁ re on Dr. Leigh, but your weapons just click as though out of ammo and nothing happens. The crew member trips on a tooth and falls into the mouth. You watch in horror as they struggle back to their feet, then glancing in your direction, their face drenched in blood, fear and confusion turning into panicked screaming as they seem to realize where they are. Then the maw slams shut to the sound of breaking bones. For several seconds you can hear bones crunching and mufﬂ ed screaming, eventually dying out with a wet gargling sound. The doctor's face resumes shape as his jaw slowly closes.
“Wonderful, I'm sure you now understand how we should conduct ourselves going forward? It's time to talk business!” The doctor turns away and slithers back further into the dusty production hall and you're too terriﬁ ed to do anything other than follow him. Erase one of your Crew Members along with their Inventory. If you have none left, your Campaign has failed and ends here.

DU:
During a long and uneventful ﬂ ight you notice your ship's speed subtly increasing without any command or input. You are still on course for the mining station where you intend to search for resources, but your concern turns into panic as you conﬁ rm that the ship's speed is increasing at a signiﬁ cant rate. Within ﬁ ve minutes the whole crew is on the bridge to bear witness as the ship exceeds light speed and the sensory equipment goes blind.
“What the hell is going on” one of your crew shouts in a panic.
“I was getting bored of waiting so I'm speeding things up”.
Everybody inside the bridge looks shocked, scanning the room in confusion, no one able to ﬁ nd where the voice came from. With a weight on their voice your second in command asks “who are you?"
“I have no need of such a thing as a name, though for the comfort of your simple mind you may refer to me as Omega”, it responds in a tone of superiority.
“Why are you here?” another crew member continues.
“For entertainment. Well, you are here for my entertainment, more accurately.”
“Right... and what are you?" The crew seem increasingly uncomfortable with the voice's presence.
“My existence extends beyond your understanding of the universe. Consider me a spectator looking for a show” the voice responds.
“A show? What kind of show? We're not a television show, we're on a critical mission!”
“I want to watch you and your crew my mortal friend, overcoming struggles and ﬁ ghting for survival. The universe is so boring if you do not ﬁ nd some distraction in the plights of the weak and feeble, no matter how unimportant those plights might be. There's only so many big things that happen, and I've seen them all a million times. So, for now I will be watching you.”
How will you respond?
A: “Well, OK. I'm sure this will be entertaining for you.
I'm going to assume you're steering the ship since we're basically blind now, so get us to that mining station and we'll give you a show.”
B: "Can you watch us in the dark?" you muse as you switch off the lights. You whisper to the crew to ignore the voice and calmly try to identify Omega somehow.

With shaky legs you continue the exploration.
DW:
You receive a long transmission sent from an unknown origin:
Adam, transmission #3:
".... I jump from world to world and despite how strange and intimidating my appearance might be to the locals I encounter, I feel that I have made more friends in this strange star system than I ever could have on Earth. My ship is more scrap and salvage than anything respectable and it will take some time until I am able to build any recognizable resistance in this system, but these new friends give me hope.
There is nothing more motivating than a cause that demands your total commitment. Unfortunately, it is still too early and too risky to establish new contacts via radio transmissions, but I can at least leave you with my report concerning the events that led up to my escape from the Mastermind.
During my months of imprisonment I was granted few views other than the walls of my cell. Occasionally I would be moved between cells or to laboratories. I have no idea where these were, whether I was on one planet or another, or maybe on a ship. I am aware that I was at times teleported to a new location. The gravity felt as consistent as my lack of freedom. The other constant was their continued experimentation, and I could see that the beings in their service were becoming increasingly like myself in their biology as they were bred and optimized more and more.
I could do nothing but eat, sleep and endure, disgusted by their experimentation but unable to do anything about it.
For whatever reason, I was given some time each day in a gigantic lavatory where I could clean myself. It became a daily ritual of mine to scrape a small sensor out of the drain. No more than a microchip and a few ﬁ ne wires, too small for me to build anything with, but still useful.
Oddly the chip I was removing would be automatically replaced each day, apparently with no one being aware of any of this occurring other than me, and I was able to use these hard chips to cut away at the inner surface of the toilet in that room. After about 200 days I was able to carve out and extract a triangular piece of solid material.
The next night as I pretended to sleep, the guard came into my cell to conduct their routine checks. Without warning I ﬂ ung the triangular shard into the guard's neck, stunning them just long enough that I could grab their Weapon. It was a tense struggle, I was exhausted from prolonged abuse, but unlike the guard I was ready for the ﬁ ght and eventually I gained the upper hand. I can't say it didn't feel good as I slammed the shard down into their chest over and over.
I couldn't use their plasma riﬂ es, but I was able to ﬁ nd some items that functioned as melee weapons. After killing a few more guards I was able to start up an escape shuttle. Rather than boarding it and attempting to escape, I launched it out on its own. As the empty craft pulled out of its berth it was almost immediately ﬁ red at, blasted into fragments. I remained behind, hiding in their recycling system. It was a perfect hiding spot, and so I remained undiscovered.
There I lived for two weeks, concealing myself among the garbage, exploring when conditions seemed relatively safe. Eventually I found a vacant production facility with a teleporter. And so it was that I was able to free myself from my imprisonment. I will never allow myself to be captured alive again, though I fear they have already got what they wanted.
Echo and off, Adam..."

As you pass near an oceanic planet you detect some Earth-code signals from beneath its thick clouds.
Following the signal, you discover a settlement built with parts of a Spanish colony ship. Big, metallic hexagonal pieces have been arranged to form houses on an island about 100km in diameter. It seems the ship was a survivor of the initial Earth migration, most of its ﬂ eet probably destroyed by the hidden Death Sphere around the solar system, or simply returning back to Earth having not been able to ﬁ nd the wormholes in the system. The residents of the settlement are indeed human, and welcome you with great enthusiasm. They recall that after arriving in this system several months ago they were almost immediately attacked by local Kraken forces and had to retreat to this planet where they could shelter beneath the thick clouds.
Their badly damaged food stocks quickly ran out, forcing them to forage and ﬁ sh for food, the only wildlife on this planet being found in this sea. It was a good source of food for a few days until they encountered a civilized species that lived in the sea, beings that wielded spears and seemed to be well organized, killing off ﬁ ve of the ﬁ shermen before they could retreat. They haven't been spotted on land yet, and it seems they breathe through gills much like ﬁ sh, so the land is considered to be safe so far.
Their eagerness in accepting the food stocks you offer them suggests that their foraging isn't a sufﬁ cient source of food, so you feel compelled to help them secure a more long term source if possible. As the sun falls they offer you a small, surprisingly fancy improvised shelter to sleep in.
A: Accept the offer and sleep in the shelter.

Earth is suffering, no time to lose! You prepare to make the jump, packing the Mastermind's information archives onto data cores to use on Earth. Then you make your best effort at aiming and activating the teleporter.
White light surrounds your view. Your mind is fractured by the bizarre experience of being everywhere for a single moment and nowhere at all for billions of years. You feel what must be eons passing by, over and over, an eternal loop in which you and all other living beings are held prisoner.
Your crew is sat in a lush green meadow at the edge of a forest. The sea glitters in the distance and a fresh breeze rustles through the leaves behind you. There's no sign of anyone else anywhere in sight. As far as you can tell, it's a beautiful day on a beautiful planet. There's no trace of pollution at all, though the sun is bigger than you remember it being, and slightly red. Is this really Earth?
The majestic trees behind you seem to be hundreds of years old. Your location seems to be a point near where you originally left Earth from, however your scanners suggest that you are actually millions of years into the future.
You open your mouth to make a comment but there are no words, no tangible thoughts inside your mind, just astonishment. The sun darkens as your gaze is drawn up towards a looming cloud, something more like a gigantic worm meandering through the horizon towards your location. Then its roar shakes the ground beneath your feet, shattering the foundations of anything that might have given you hope. The technology of thousands of years would be irrelevant in the shadow of millions of years of evolution. Your Campaign has failed and ends here.
